accepted.s: The Regional Rural Banks were initially created through an ordinance before being placed under which legislation?
accepted.x: Regional Rural Banks were initially created through an ordinance and were subsequently governed by the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
accepted.tq: Test the legislative sequence rather than recalling only the year of establishment.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the role of the sponsor bank of a Regional Rural Bank?
o: It provides capital, technology and management support.
It supervises the RRB in place of NABARD.
It alone owns the entire share capital of the RRB.
It fixes the statutory priority-sector target of the RRB.
accepted.x: The sponsor public sector bank provides capital, technology and management support to the RRB. NABARD supervises RRBs, while the RBI regulates them.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who performs this function?’ method to distinguish sponsor-bank functions from regulatory functions.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s:
With reference to the ownership pattern of Regional Rural Banks, consider the following statements:
1. The Central Government holds 50 per cent of the share capital.
2. The sponsor bank holds 35 per cent of the share capital.
3. The concerned State Government holds 15 per cent of the share capital.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The ownership pattern of an RRB is Centre 50 per cent, sponsor bank 35 per cent and State Government 15 per cent.
accepted.tq: Check the complete numerical composition before selecting the coded option.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the regulatory and supervisory arrangement for Regional Rural Banks?
accepted.x: RRBs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India and supervised by NABARD.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure institutional pair and eliminate options that interchange regulatory roles.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: As a result of the ‘One State-One RRB’ amalgamation exercise, how many RRBs were amalgamated with effect from 1 May 2025?
accepted.x: Fifteen RRBs were amalgamated with effect from 1 May 2025 under the One State-One RRB initiative, leaving 28 RRBs thereafter.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the number amalgamated from the number remaining after amalgamation.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the four Andhra Pradesh Regional Rural Banks merged into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank?
accepted.x: The four merged RRBs were Andhra Pragathi, AP Grameena Vikas, Chaitanya Godavari and Saptagiri. Krishna Tungabhadra Grameena Bank was not included in the stated list.
accepted.tq: Find the odd institution by checking every member of the named merger list.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the reported FY26 position of Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank?
o: Business ₹1,36,337 crore and net profit ₹836 crore
Business ₹1,36,337 crore and net profit ₹1,836 crore
Business ₹1,83,637 crore and net profit ₹1,336 crore
Business ₹13,633 crore and net profit ₹18,360 crore
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank reported FY26 business of ₹1,36,337 crore and net profit of ₹1,836 crore.
accepted.tq: Separate closely placed digits in the business and profit figures.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Service Area Approach introduced in 1989?
o: Each bank branch is restricted to financing only one crop.
Each State is assigned one commercial bank for all credit operations.
Each rural branch prepares credit plans for a designated group of villages.
Each district is assigned a separate RBI banking circle.
accepted.x: Under the Service Area Approach, each rural bank branch plans credit for a specified set of villages.
accepted.tq: Match the approach with its operational unit and area of responsibility.
accepted.sec: Lead Bank Scheme - Service Area Approach, SLBC, AP convener bank

accepted.s: At which level does the State Level Bankers’ Committee function?
accepted.x: The State Level Bankers’ Committee is a State-level forum, while district-level forums are run by the Lead District Manager.
accepted.tq: Use the name of the institution to distinguish State-level and district-level forums.
accepted.sec: Lead Bank Scheme - Service Area Approach, SLBC, AP convener bank

accepted.s: Who conducts the district-level forums under the Lead Bank Scheme?
o: The State Level Bankers’ Committee convener
accepted.x: District-level forums under the Lead Bank Scheme are conducted by the Lead District Manager.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to identify the district-level coordinator.
accepted.sec: Lead Bank Scheme - Service Area Approach, SLBC, AP convener bank

accepted.s: Which bank acts as the Lead Bank and SLBC convener in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Union Bank of India acts as the Lead Bank and the convener of the State Level Bankers’ Committee in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Test the specific State-level institutional assignment rather than the general Lead Bank concept.
accepted.sec: Lead Bank Scheme - Service Area Approach, SLBC, AP convener bank

accepted.s: The 236th meeting of the Andhra Pradesh State Level Bankers’ Committee was held on
accepted.x: The 236th SLBC meeting in Andhra Pradesh was held on 16 September 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the meeting date from the date on which it was reported.
accepted.sec: Lead Bank Scheme - Service Area Approach, SLBC, AP convener bank

accepted.s: A bank included in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and having the prescribed minimum paid-up capital and reserves is known as a
accepted.x: Scheduled banks are those included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934. They must have paid-up capital and reserves of at least ₹5 lakh.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal classification from the statutory schedule and eligibility condition.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: Which of the following facilities may be available to a scheduled bank under the stated banking structure?
o: Borrowing from the RBI at bank rate, repo rate or through MSF
Accepting deposits without maintaining any reserves
Lending exclusively to the agricultural sector
accepted.x: Scheduled banks may borrow from the RBI at the bank rate, repo rate or through the Marginal Standing Facility, subject to applicable conditions.
accepted.tq: Choose the option describing a banking facility rather than an exclusive or absolute power.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct short-term co-operative credit structure?
accepted.x: The short-term co-operative credit structure progresses from Primary Agricultural Credit Societies to District Central Co-operative Banks and then to the State Co-operative Bank.
accepted.tq: Arrange the institutions from the grassroots level to the State level.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: Which principle is associated with the governance of co-operative banks?
accepted.x: Co-operative banks follow the principle of one member, one vote.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the co-operative voting principle from share-based corporate voting.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: The associate banks of the State Bank of India and Bharatiya Mahila Bank were merged into SBI on
accepted.x: The associate banks of SBI and Bharatiya Mahila Bank were merged into SBI with effect from 1 April 2017.
accepted.tq: Use the year-specific merger date to distinguish closely spaced alternatives.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: Foreign banks may operate in India in which of the following forms?
o: Only as branches of the RBI
accepted.x: Foreign banks may operate in India either through branches or as wholly owned subsidiaries.
accepted.tq: Reject options containing exclusive words when the legal framework permits more than one form.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: The permitted foreign direct investment limit in private sector banks, as stated for 2004, was
accepted.x: The stated FDI limit in private sector banks was raised to 74 per cent in 2004.
accepted.tq: Select the precise percentage from the banking-ownership alternatives.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding non-banking financial companies:
1. They cannot accept demand deposits.
2. They cannot issue cheques drawn on themselves.
3. Their deposits are not insured by the DICGC.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits or issue cheques, and their deposits are not covered by DICGC insurance.
accepted.tq: Test all three distinguishing features of NBFCs before choosing the combined code.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation was formed in 1978 by merging which two institutions?
accepted.x: DICGC was formed in 1978 through the merger of the Deposit Insurance Corporation and the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with its constituent predecessor organisations.
accepted.sec: RRBs - origin committee, first RRB, sponsor bank, AP RRBs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes payments banks from small finance banks?
o: Payments banks can lend, whereas SFBs cannot lend.
SFBs are exclusively owned by State Governments.
Payments banks accept deposits but cannot lend, whereas SFBs promote financial inclusion.
Both types of banks are prohibited from accepting deposits.
accepted.x: Payments banks can accept deposits but cannot lend. Small finance banks were established primarily to promote financial inclusion.
accepted.tq: Separate the paired banking models by their lending and inclusion functions.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: Which one of the following is classified as an organised source of finance?
accepted.x: RRBs are part of the organised financial system. Moneylenders and indigenous bankers are unorganised sources.
accepted.tq: Separate formal financial institutions from traditional informal lenders.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: As reported for July 2026, the number of operational small finance banks in India was
accepted.x: There were 11 operational small finance banks as reported for July 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the category-specific count and avoid confusing it with the RRB or UCB count.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the banking-outlet coverage of inhabited villages?
accepted.x: It was reported that 99.92 per cent of inhabited villages had a banking outlet within 5 km.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a near-complete coverage figure from the absolute claim of 100 per cent.
accepted.sec: Banking structure - scheduled vs non-scheduled, commercial, RRBs, co-operative, SBI group, foreign bank entry

accepted.s: What is the priority-sector lending target for domestic banks and eligible foreign banks?
accepted.x: Domestic banks and eligible foreign banks have a priority-sector lending target of 40 per cent of Adjusted Net Bank Credit.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the general bank target from the higher RRB and SFB target.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: The priority-sector lending target prescribed for Regional Rural Banks and Small Finance Banks is
accepted.x: RRBs and SFBs have a priority-sector lending target of 75 per cent of ANBC.
accepted.tq: Compare institution-specific targets instead of applying the domestic-bank target universally.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the agricultural sub-targets within priority-sector lending?
o: Agriculture 40 per cent; non-corporate farmers 18 per cent; small and marginal farmers 14 per cent
Agriculture 14 per cent; non-corporate farmers 18 per cent; small and marginal farmers 10 per cent
Agriculture 18 per cent; non-corporate farmers 14 per cent; small and marginal farmers 10 per cent
Agriculture 10 per cent; non-corporate farmers 14 per cent; small and marginal farmers 18 per cent
accepted.x: The stated agricultural target is 18 per cent, including 14 per cent for non-corporate farmers and 10 per cent for small and marginal farmers.
accepted.tq: Read the nested targets carefully and avoid reversing the percentage rows.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the stated priority-sector categories?
accepted.x: Priority-sector categories include agriculture, MSME, export credit, education, housing, social infrastructure and renewable energy, among others. Luxury consumer goods are not listed.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the recognised priority-sector list.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: A bank that has fallen short of its priority-sector lending target can meet the shortfall by
o: purchasing Priority Sector Lending Certificates from a bank with a surplus
transferring its deposits to a foreign bank
purchasing government securities from the RBI
accepted.x: A bank short of its priority-sector target may purchase PSLCs from banks that have exceeded their targets.
accepted.tq: Apply the surplus-deficit mechanism to identify the function of PSLCs.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the EAC-PM paper on priority-sector lending:
1. It found that about 7–8 per cent of districts received approximately 45–46 per cent of PSL credit.
2. It criticised reliance on Priority Sector Lending Certificates.
3. It recommended a review of the 40 per cent priority-sector target.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The EAC-PM paper reported the concentration of PSL credit in a small share of districts, criticised reliance on PSLCs and called for a review of the 40 per cent target.
accepted.tq: Combine the finding, criticism and recommendation before selecting the coded answer.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey 2025–26, priority-sector lending constituted what percentage of ANBC in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Priority-sector lending in Andhra Pradesh was reported at 63.28 per cent of ANBC.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the State-level actual figure from the national target percentages.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh Socio-Economic Survey 2025–26, agriculture accounted for what percentage of ANBC under priority-sector lending?
accepted.x: Agriculture accounted for 42.11 per cent of ANBC under priority-sector lending in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Separate the Andhra Pradesh actual share from the national agricultural sub-target of 18 per cent.
accepted.sec: Priority sector lending - targets, sub-targets, PSLCs

accepted.s: The production credit of Andhra Pradesh’s rural co-operative credit system in 2025–26 was reported as
accepted.x: Production credit in 2025–26 was reported at ₹4,607.22 crore.
accepted.tq: Check both the unit and the placement of the decimal before selecting the amount.

o: 1.65 lakh bank branches, 17.36 lakh business correspondents and 1.81 lakh IPPB centres
17.36 lakh bank branches, 1.81 lakh business correspondents and 1.65 lakh IPPB centres
1.81 lakh bank branches, 17.36 lakh business correspondents and 1.65 lakh IPPB centres
1.81 lakh bank branches, 1.736 lakh business correspondents and 17.65 lakh IPPB centres
accepted.x: The reported figures were 1.81 lakh bank branches, 17.36 lakh business correspondents and 1.65 lakh India Post Payments Bank centres.
accepted.tq: Match the three figures with the correct infrastructure categories.

accepted.x: The reported figures were 1,457 Urban Cooperative Banks and 28 RRBs.
